name: punctuation
title: Spanish Punctuation Practice: ¿ ¡, Commas, Dashes and Quotes
description: Practice Spanish punctuation: opening ¿ and ¡, commas, the dash in dialogue, quotation marks, numbers and capitals, with a rule table and 10 checked sentences.
answer: Spanish opens questions and exclamations with ¿ and ¡ and closes them with ? and !, placed exactly where the question starts. Dialogue uses a long dash (—) instead of quotation marks. Days, months and languages are lowercase. Many Spanish-speaking countries use a comma for decimals and a period for thousands, but Mexico and the US use the English system.

demand.source: Google autocomplete for US searchers (hl=en, gl=us), docs/seo-plan/us1000/suggest-us-20261127b.csv

rules.use: Question only on part of the sentence

rules.example: el lunes 3 de mayo; hablo español

quiz.why: The ¿ goes where the question starts, after the comma.
Days of the week are lowercase.
Dialogue starts with a dash: —¿Tienes hambre?
Spanish letters use a colon after the greeting: Querida Ana:
Each exclamation needs its own opening ¡.
Months stay lowercase, even in dates.

mistakes: Leaving out the opening ¿ or ¡: Spanish writes both marks, even in short questions (¿Sí?).
Capitalizing days, months and languages: «el Lunes 5 de Mayo» should be «el lunes 5 de mayo».
Putting ¿ at the start of the sentence when only part is a question: «Si llueve, ¿vienes?»
Using quotation marks for dialogue as in English: Spanish novels and many texts use dashes (—).
Using a comma after the greeting of a letter: formal Spanish uses a colon: «Estimado señor:».

heritage: Heritage speakers often skip ¿ and ¡ on phones and capitalize months and days by English habit. Those are the two punctuation errors teachers mark most in heritage writing. Setting a Spanish keyboard on your phone makes ¿ and ¡ one tap away.
teacher: Give students a short dialogue copied with English punctuation. In pairs, they rewrite it with dashes, ¿ ¡ and lowercase months, then read it aloud as a scene.

faq.question: Why does Spanish use upside-down question marks?
faq.answer: So the reader knows from the start that a question or exclamation is coming, which matters because Spanish questions often have the same word order as statements: ¿Tu hermano trabaja aquí? The rule dates from 1754.

faq.question: Are days and months capitalized in Spanish?
faq.answer: No. Days of the week, months, seasons and languages are lowercase: el lunes, en mayo, en verano, hablo inglés. They take a capital only at the start of a sentence or in titles.

faq.question: How is dialogue punctuated in Spanish?
faq.answer: With a long dash (—) at the start of each line and around the narrator's words: —Ya voy —dijo Marta—, espera un momento. Quotation marks are used for quotes inside the text.
